# Fun Language

> Fun is a ~0.3 MB, zero-dependency scripting language that spans JSON and FD data, daily glue code, FFI, runtime C, JIT and raw machine code. This file is the AI entry point.

Ontology v0.1.0 for Fun 9.5.7.

## Start here

- [Language tutorial](https://funlang.org/docs/tutorial.md): task-oriented walkthrough
- [Standard library](https://funlang.org/docs/standard-library.md): module map and edge cases
- [Full manual](https://funlang.org/man.htm): chapter-by-chapter reference
- [Full ontology text](https://funlang.org/ontology/llms-full.txt): every concept and example

## Core concepts

- [syntax.hello](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.hello): Hello world. A Fun script is a sequence of statements; `?.` prints a value and a newline.
- [syntax.statement](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.statement): Statements and semicolons. Statements end with `;`. The `;` after a block closer (`end if`, `end fun`, `end class`, `end do`, `end loop`, `end try`) is optional, and the last statement before `}` may omit it. Newlines are not statement boundaries.
- [syntax.comment](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.comment): Comments. Both `#` and `//` start a line comment. `#* ... #` is a block comment; the next `#` closes it.
- [syntax.var](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.var): Variables. Declare with `var name = expr;` or `var name;` (nil). There is no `let` or `const`; identifiers are case-insensitive.
- [syntax.assignment](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.assignment): Assignment and equality. A statement `x = expr;` assigns; the same `=` inside an expression compares. `<>` and `!=` both mean not-equal. Compound assignment uses `+= -= *= &=`.
- [syntax.print](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.print): Print and output. Bare `?` prints with no separator, `?.` with a newline, `?,` with a space, and `?:` with a tab. All four accept any value.
- [syntax.function](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.function): Named functions. A `fun name(params) ... end fun;` returns the value assigned to `result`; `return expr;` exits early. A one-expression function can also be written `var name(a, b) = expr;`. `result` is not reset on entry, so initialize it explicitly.
- [syntax.lambda](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.lambda): Lambdas. The arrow forms `a -> expr` and `(a, b) -> expr` return an expression. For a block body use `fun (a, b) { ... }` with `return` or `result`; a bare `{ ... }` is a zero-argument block function.
- [syntax.if](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.if): Conditionals. The form `if c then ... elsif c2 then ... else ... end if;` supports branches. The shorthand `if c { ... }` is a single branch only and takes no `elsif` or `else`.
- [syntax.case](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.case): Case. The form `case expr is when v do ... else ... end case;` matches values.
- [syntax.loop](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.loop): Loops. Forms: `for i = a to b do ... end do;`, `for k: v in set do ... end do;`, `while c do ... end do;`, and `loop ... exit when c; ... end loop;`. `while c loop ... end loop;` and `for ... loop ... end loop;` are accepted equivalents; `while c { ... }` and `for ... { ... }` are single-block shorthands. `next when c;` skips.
- [syntax.try](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.try): Errors. The form `try ... except ... finally ... end try;` catches `raise` and runtime errors. `runtime.lastError()` exposes message, file, line and stack.
- [syntax.class](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.class): Classes. A `class Name(params) ... end class;` body runs as the constructor; `var` fields become members, `fun` declarations become methods, `this` is the instance and `base` the parent. Inherit with `class Child = Parent()`.
- [syntax.use](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.use): Modules. The statement `use 'lib-set.fun';` links a module by file name; `use 'x.fun' as ns;` namespaces it. Paths resolve relative to the script and the runtime `lib/` directory.
- [syntax.collection](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.collection): Lists and maps. A list literal `[1, 2, 3]` is a list. `new [k: v]` is a string-keyed map (called a set in Fun); `new []` is an empty map, while `new [1, 2]` builds a fresh list. Both support `@count`, `@has`, `@add`, and JSON conversion.
- [syntax.member](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.member): Member access. Forms `obj.key`, `obj['key']` and `obj.['1']` read members; a missing member compares equal to nil. Postfix `?` makes a member or its base optional: `x?.k?`.
- [syntax.method](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.method): Built-in methods. Engine-provided methods use `@`: `x.@toJson()`, `s.@count()`, `m.@('group')`. Methods you write in a class are called without `@`.
- [syntax.pipe](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.pipe): Pipe. The pipe `value | f` passes the value as the last argument of `f`. `map(f)` takes the list last, so it composes; `filter(list, f)` takes the list first, so call it directly.
- [syntax.string](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.string): Strings. Single, double and backtick quotes all delimit strings. Literals do not decode backslash escapes; call `.escape()` to decode `\n`, `\t`, etc., use `10.toChar()`, or use a multiline backtick string. `$name` interpolation is done by `.eval()`.
- [syntax.regex](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.regex): Regular expressions. Regex literals are `/pattern/flags`, `%pattern%flags` or `$'pattern'flags`. Use `=~` / `!~` to test, `.match()` to extract, `.replace()` to rewrite.
- [syntax.json](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.json): JSON. The built-in `value.@toJson()` emits JSON; `value.@toJson(json: true)` quotes keys. Parse with `text.getJson(json: true)`. `text.getJson(fd: true)` parses FD.
- [syntax.fd](https://funlang.org/ontology/#syntax.fd): FD data. FD is Fun's indentation data notation: `key value` lines, `- item` lists, no braces. `text.getJson(fd: true)` parses it and `value.@toJson(fd: true)` emits it.
- [sem.missing-is-nil](https://funlang.org/ontology/#sem.missing-is-nil): Missing values compare to nil. Reading a missing member, key or index yields a value that compares equal to nil. This makes `if x = nil then x = init; end if` safe.
- [sem.nil-arithmetic](https://funlang.org/ontology/#sem.nil-arithmetic): nil acts as zero in arithmetic. A nil operand in `+ - * / div mod` is treated as 0, and as '' for strings. `x += 1` therefore works on a fresh key. The flip side is that a missing value also compares equal to 0.
- [sem.or-value](https://funlang.org/ontology/#sem.or-value): or/and return values. Operators `or` and `and` return one of their operands, Lua style: `nil or 5` is 5, `7 or 5` is 7. This powers default values.
- [sem.result](https://funlang.org/ontology/#sem.result): result is not reset. Each function has one `result` slot. It is not cleared on entry, so a call at the same stack depth can see the previous value. Always initialize `result`.
- [sem.case-insensitive](https://funlang.org/ontology/#sem.case-insensitive): Identifiers are case-insensitive. Variables, functions, members and built-in method names all fold case. Avoid local names that differ from another symbol only by case.
- [sem.named-args](https://funlang.org/ontology/#sem.named-args): Named arguments. Call sites may name arguments: `f(b: 2, a: 1)`. Missing arguments are nil, so defaults are written as `if p = nil then p = default; end if`.
- [idiom.default](https://funlang.org/ontology/#idiom.default): Default value. Use `or` to supply a default for nil or false. `x = x or default;`.
- [idiom.accumulator](https://funlang.org/ontology/#idiom.accumulator): Safe accumulator. Seed a counter explicitly when you want the intent to be obvious across builds: `m.k = (m.k or 0) + 1;`. On 9.5.7, `m.k += 1` also yields 1.
- [idiom.pipeline](https://funlang.org/ontology/#idiom.pipeline): Data pipeline. The pipeline `xs | map(f)` reads left to right. Add `use 'lib-set.fun';` first. `map` takes the list last and composes; `filter` takes the list first.
- [idiom.json-roundtrip](https://funlang.org/ontology/#idiom.json-roundtrip): JSON round trip. Parse with `.getJson(json: true)`, inspect with member access, emit with `.@toJson(json: true)`.
- [pit.double-equals](https://funlang.org/ontology/#pit.double-equals): There is no ==. Use `=` for equality inside an expression, and `<>` or `!=` for inequality. `==` is not Fun.
- [pit.newline-is-not-a-statement](https://funlang.org/ontology/#pit.newline-is-not-a-statement): Newlines do not end statements. A newline is whitespace. Put `;` between statements; a continuation line can silently join the previous expression.
- [pit.backslash-escape](https://funlang.org/ontology/#pit.backslash-escape): Literals do not decode backslash escapes. The literal `'\n'` is a backslash followed by `n`, not a newline. Call `.escape()` to decode it, or use `10.toChar()` or a multiline backtick string.
- [pit.missing-key-accumulate](https://funlang.org/ontology/#pit.missing-key-accumulate): A missing value also equals zero. A missing value compares equal to nil and to 0, so `if x = 0` cannot tell "absent" from "zero". Use `.@has(key)` when presence matters.
- [pit.array-vs-map](https://funlang.org/ontology/#pit.array-vs-map): [] is a list, new [] is a map. A list literal `[1, 2]` is ordered; `new [a: 1]` is a string-keyed map and `new []` is an empty map, but `new [1, 2]` is a list. Do not use `{}` for either.
- [pit.return-keyword](https://funlang.org/ontology/#pit.return-keyword): result vs return. Inside `fun`, assigning `result` sets the return value; `return expr;` returns immediately. A bare `return;` returns the current `result`, which may be stale.
- [tool.funcmd](https://funlang.org/ontology/#tool.funcmd): The fun command. The command `fun file.fun` runs a script; `fun test` runs a package's tests; `fun pack` builds one executable; `fun package init` creates a manifest.
- [module.lib-set](https://funlang.org/ontology/#module.lib-set): lib-set. Collection helpers in pure Fun: `map`, `filter`, `find`, `sort`, `compose`, `range`, `@clone`, and more.
- [module.lib-json](https://funlang.org/ontology/#module.lib-json): lib-json. JSON and FD parse/stringify helpers. The underlying built-ins are `.getJson()` and `.@toJson()`, documented in `lib-json.fun`.
- [builtin.tojson](https://funlang.org/ontology/#builtin.tojson): @toJson. The built-in serializer. Default output is JSON-like with bare keys; `json: true` quotes keys, and `fd: true` emits FD.
- [builtin.escape](https://funlang.org/ontology/#builtin.escape): .escape(). Decodes backslash escapes in a string: `'\n'.escape()` is a newline, `'\t'.escape()` a tab. Literals keep the backslash until `.escape()` is called.
- [task.json-transform](https://funlang.org/ontology/#task.json-transform): Transform JSON. Parse a JSON document, update a nested value, and emit JSON again.

The full index is in llms-full.txt.
